abstract:
<jats:p>
                  <jats:bold>The aim of the work is studying the aeroelastic response of the
15 MW NREL-IEA large-scale wind turbine using a high-fidelity
fluid-structure interaction solver that combines large-eddy simulation
with a modal computational structural dynamics solver through a two-way
coupling. The fluid solver employs the actuator line model to simulate
the interaction between the turbine blades and the fluid and the
immersed boundary method to model the presence of the tower and nacelle.
The results are compared with those obtained by the OpenFAST software,
which is a well-known numerical tool for engineering predictions. A
series of simulations have been performed with and without the presence
of the tower and nacelle to better understand the effects of these
components on flow structures and structural deformations. The largest
discrepancies among the solvers have been observed in correspondence
with the blade passage in front of the tower, which induces an abrupt
alteration in the local incidence angle of the flow.</jats:bold>
                </jats:p>
title: Large Eddy Simulation of the IEA 15-MW Wind Turbine Using a Two-Way Coupled Fluid-Structure Interaction Model
